steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package to enable component creation and state management for the hiring interview application.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and hooks
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode:
// No code yet — this is the first step.
// Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React dependencies are imported, allowing you to create components and manage state.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, setting up the foundation for building the hiring interview application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. Please import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the HiringDashboard component
steps.instruction: Create a functional React component named HiringDashboard that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define the component using either a function declaration or arrow function syntax, and make sure it returns a div element.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the HiringDashboard component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A HiringDashboard component is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: The component is named HiringDashboard and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the foundation for the hiring dashboard component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly HiringDashboard and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check the name and return statement.

steps.title: Initialize candidate data state
steps.instruction: Inside the HiringDashboard component, use useState to create a state variable named 'candidates' initialized with an array of candidate objects. Each object should have id, name, role, and interviewStage properties.
steps.hint: Initialize useState with an array containing at least one candidate object. Example: { id: 1, name: 'Alex Chen', role: 'Frontend Engineer', interviewStage: 'Technical' }
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a candidates state variable containing an array of candidate objects with the required properties.
successCriteria: candidates state is declared with useState, initialized with an array of objects, and each object has id, name, role, and interviewStage properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the candidates state with hiring data. This gives us a foundation to build our hiring dashboard UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track with state initialization. Make sure your candidates array contains at least one complete candidate object with all four required properties: id, name, role, and interviewStage.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on initializing the candidates state. Use useState to create a state variable named 'candidates' initialized with an array of objects containing id, name, role, and interviewStage properties.

steps.title: Initialize filter state
steps.instruction: Inside the HiringDashboard component, use useState to create a state variable named 'roleFilter' initialized to an empty string.
steps.hint: Add a useState call that returns a state variable and setter function, similar to how you initialized the candidates state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing a filter state
const [filter, setFilter] = useState('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a roleFilter state variable ready to track the current role filter value.
successCriteria: A roleFilter state variable is declared using useState and initialized to an empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the roleFilter state. This will allow you to filter candidates by their role in upcoming steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to declare a state variable named 'roleFilter' with an initial value of an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires initializing a roleFilter state variable using useState. Please add: const [roleFilter, setRoleFilter] = useState(''); inside the component.

steps.title: Define filter handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the HiringDashboard component, create a function named handleFilterChange that takes a newFilter parameter and updates the roleFilter state with it.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setRoleFilter with the provided newFilter value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleFilterChange function is defined that updates the roleFilter state when called with a new filter value.
successCriteria: The component contains a handleFilterChange function that accepts a parameter and calls setRoleFilter with it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the filter handler function that will update the roleFilter state when the user interacts with filter controls.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function accepts a parameter and calls setRoleFilter with it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function named handleFilterChange that takes a parameter and updates the roleFilter state.

steps.title: Define stage update handler
steps.instruction: Inside your HiringDashboard component, create a function named handleStageUpdate that takes candidateId and newStage as parameters and updates the candidate's interviewStage in the candidates state.
steps.hint: You'll need to use setCandidates to update the state. Map through the candidates array and update the matching candidate's interviewStage.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleStageUpdate function is defined that properly updates a candidate's interview stage when provided with their ID and the new stage.
successCriteria: The handleStageUpdate function is defined with candidateId and newStage parameters, uses setCandidates to update state, and correctly maps through candidates to update the matching candidate.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the stage update handler that will allow you to track candidate progression through interview stages.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function properly updates the candidates state using setCandidates and the map method to find and update the correct candidate.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create handleStageUpdate with two parameters and use setCandidates to update the state by mapping through candidates.

steps.title: Add dashboard container structure
steps.instruction: Inside the HiringDashboard component, replace the current return statement with a main container div containing a header element with the title 'Hiring Dashboard'.
steps.hint: Return a JSX structure with a main div wrapper and a header element inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a basic container structure with a header containing the dashboard title.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a main div wrapper
The div contains a header element
The header contains the text 'Hiring Dashboard'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the basic container structure for the hiring dashboard. This provides the foundation for adding candidate data and filtering controls.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have a main div container with a header element inside that displays 'Hiring Dashboard'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The structure doesn't match the requirements. You need to replace the return statement with a div containing a header with the title 'Hiring Dashboard'.

steps.title: Add filter controls section
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add a <section> element with a heading 'Filter Candidates' and a <select> dropdown for role filtering. The select should have an onChange event wired to handleFilterChange and its value bound to roleFilter state.
steps.hint: Add the section after the return statement. Include a <label> for the select with appropriate text.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: filter section with dropdown

Filter Options
steps.expectedOutcome: A filter section with a heading and a role filter dropdown is added to the component's UI structure.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a <section> with a heading 'Filter Candidates' and a <select> element wired to handleFilterChange and roleFilter state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the filter controls section with proper event wiring and state binding.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some filter controls, but check that you have the heading, select element, onChange handler, and value binding all correctly implemented.
steps.feedbackWrong: The filter controls section is missing or incomplete. Review the instruction to add the section with heading and select dropdown.

steps.title: Add candidates display section
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add a <section> element with a heading 'Candidates' and a <ul> that maps through the candidates array to display each candidate's name, role, and current stage.
steps.hint: Use the map() method on the candidates array to create a list item for each candidate. Display the candidate's properties inside the list item.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display a candidates section with a list of candidate details when the candidates array has data.
successCriteria: A <section> element with a heading and a <ul> that maps through candidates is added to the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the candidates display section. This shows how to render state data dynamically in the UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some structure, but make sure to include the heading, the <ul> element, and the map() method to iterate through candidates.
steps.feedbackWrong: The candidates display section is missing or incomplete. Please add a <section> with a heading and a <ul> that maps through the candidates array.

steps.title: Add stage progression buttons
steps.instruction: Inside the candidates display section, for each candidate, add buttons to move between interview stages: 'Phone Screen', 'Technical', 'Behavioral', and 'Offer'. Wire each button's onClick event to call handleStageUpdate with the candidate's id and the target stage.
steps.hint: Map over the candidates array and render buttons for each stage. Pass the candidate id and the target stage string to handleStageUpdate when clicked.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each candidate in the display section will have four buttons representing interview stages, allowing users to simulate moving candidates through the hiring pipeline.
successCriteria: Buttons for 'Phone Screen', 'Technical', 'Behavioral', and 'Offer' are rendered for each candidate with onClick handlers that call handleStageUpdate with the candidate id and target stage.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added stage progression buttons for each candidate, creating an interactive hiring workflow interface.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some buttons, but make sure all four stage buttons are present for each candidate and properly wired to handleStageUpdate with the correct parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The stage progression buttons are missing or not properly configured. Each candidate needs four buttons with onClick handlers that call handleStageUpdate with the candidate id and target stage.
